tasks.content:
À partir des informations d'issue #951 : 'Breakout un jeu basé sur appshell' — le jeu arcade classique avec mur de briques, balle rebondissante, raquette et 3 vies.

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/product-spec.md.

Il doit contenir :
- **product name** : Breakout
- **problem statement** : Jeu arcade où le joueur détruit un mur de briques en contrôlant une raquette pour faire rebondir une balle
- **target user** : Joueurs de jeux arcade
- **primary capabilities** (V1) :
  1. Moteur de jeu avec balle rebondissante et détection de collision AABB
  2. Raquette contrôlée au clavier (flèches gauche/droite)
  3. Mur de 5 lignes de briques destructibles
  4. Système de vies (3 au départ, perte si la balle descend sous l'écran)
  5. Victoire/Défaite (destruction complète du mur = victoire, 0 vies = défaite)
  6. Menu avec sliders pour régler la vitesse de la balle (lente à rapide)
  7. Navigation menus à la souris (démarrer, rejouer, quitter)
- **technical stack** : React + Vite, Canvas 2D, AppShell
- **key constraints** : Game loop avec requestAnimationFrame et delta time, Détection de collision AABB

SITE_DESCRIPTION doit être une phrase unique (max 160 chars) décrivant le produit.

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/epic.md.

L'épic MVP doit couvrir la V1 complète du jeu Breakout tel que décrit dans product-spec.md. Les sections principales :
- Vision : délivrer un jeu Breakout fonctionnel jouable
- Scope : V1 = toutes les capacités listées dans product-spec
- User stories : 4-5 US couvrant gameplay principal, menus et système de vies
- Acceptance criteria : jeu jouable, sensations de gameplay fluides, pas de crash

Le fichier doit lister les user stories dans une section 'Composant User Stories' (sans les créer — elles seront produites par la tâche suivante).

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md et apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/user-stories/us-001-gameplay-mechanics.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/us.md.

User Story: US-001 — Gameplay Mechanics (moteur de jeu principal)

Format Mike Cohn :
- Title: Gameplay Mechanics
- As a player
- I want to play a game where a ball bounces off walls, paddle, and bricks with physics-based collisions
- So that I experience classic Breakout arcade mechanics

Acceptance criteria (Gherkin format) :
- Given the game is running, When the ball moves, Then it bounces off walls and paddle with correct trajectory
- Given a brick exists, When the ball hits it, Then the brick is destroyed
- Given the paddle is hit by the ball, When the player moves the paddle, Then the ball direction changes
- Given no bricks remain, When all bricks are destroyed, Then the player wins
- Given the ball falls below the screen, When it happens, Then the player loses one life

Doit inclure : description technique (Canvas 2D, requestAnimationFrame, delta time, AABB collision detection), risques techniques, estimation story points.

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md et apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/user-stories/us-002-paddle-control.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/us.md.

User Story: US-002 — Paddle Control

Format Mike Cohn :
- Title: Paddle Control
- As a player
- I want to control the paddle exclusively with left/right keyboard arrows
- So that I can hit the ball and keep it in play

Acceptance criteria (Gherkin format) :
- Given the game is running, When I press the left arrow key, Then the paddle moves left
- Given the game is running, When I press the right arrow key, Then the paddle moves right
- Given the paddle is at the left boundary, When I press left, Then the paddle does not move further
- Given the paddle is at the right boundary, When I press right, Then the paddle does not move further
- Given the game is paused, When I press arrow keys, Then nothing happens

Doit inclure : description technique (event listeners, input handling, paddle bounds), estimation story points.

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md et apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/user-stories/us-003-lives-and-menus.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/us.md.

User Story: US-003 — Lives System & Menus

Format Mike Cohn :
- Title: Lives System & Menus
- As a player
- I want to start with 3 lives, lose a life when the ball falls off the bottom, and see menu options to start, replay, and quit
- So that I can manage the game flow and replay after game over

Acceptance criteria (Gherkin format) :
- Given the game starts, When I load the game, Then I have 3 lives
- Given a life is active, When the ball falls below the screen, Then I lose one life
- Given I have lost all lives, When lives reach 0, Then the game ends with 'Game Over' screen
- Given the game ends, When the win/lose state is reached, Then I can click 'Replay' or 'Quit'
- Given the game is running, When I click 'Pause', Then the game pauses and shows the pause menu
- Given the pause menu is open, When I click 'Resume', Then the game resumes

Doit inclure : description technique (state management, menu components, mouse input handling), estimation story points.

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md et apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md

Crée apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/user-stories/us-004-speed-settings.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/us.md.

User Story: US-004 — Ball Speed Settings

Format Mike Cohn :
- Title: Ball Speed Settings
- As a player
- I want to adjust the ball speed before the game starts via a slider (from very slow to very fast)
- So that I can control the game difficulty

Acceptance criteria (Gherkin format) :
- Given the main menu is open, When I see the speed slider, Then it ranges from 'Very Slow' to 'Very Fast'
- Given I adjust the slider, When I change the value, Then the ball speed updates accordingly
- Given the game is running, When I started with a speed setting, Then the ball maintains that speed
- Given the slider is at its minimum, When the game plays, Then the ball moves slowly
- Given the slider is at its maximum, When the game plays, Then the ball moves very fast

Doit inclure : description technique (slider component, speed parameter binding), estimation story points.

Lis apps/breakout/docs/what/product-spec.md, apps/breakout/docs/what/epics/epic-0-mvp/epic.md et tous les fichiers user-stories créés.

Crée apps/breakout/docs/how/architecture.md en utilisant le template .oneticket/templates/architecture.md.

L'architecture doit décrire :

1. **Technical Stack** : React + Vite + TypeScript, Canvas 2D, AppShell foundation
2. **System Overview** : Single-page game app avec Canvas au centre, React UI pour menus et HUD
3. **Core Components** :
   - GameEngine : moteur principal (game loop, physics, collision)
   - GameCanvas : composant React wrappant le Canvas via useRef
   - UI Layer : menus (Main, Pause, GameOver), HUD (lives display, speed indicator)
   - Input Handler : keyboard + mouse événements
   - State Management : game state (running, paused, over), lives, score, ball speed

4. **Data Flow** :
   - GameEngine produit l'état du jeu à chaque frame
   - UI Layer consomme cet état via props/context
   - Input Handler → GameEngine (commands)
   - Canvas rendering synchronisé avec delta time

5. **Key Constraints** :
   - Game loop via requestAnimationFrame (60fps target)
   - Collision detection : AABB entre ball, paddle, bricks, walls
   - Performance : minimiser re-renders React en séparant Canvas du reste
   - Responsive : Canvas adaptatif au viewport

6. **Persistence & State** :
   - localStorage pour sauvegarder speed slider preference

Le fichier doit mapper chaque user story à un/plusieurs composant(s) technique(s).
